theories.title: EDF as an explicit diagnostic representation
theories.statement: EDF is a coherent grammar for expressing a context-bound diagnostic model that separates observation, candidate origins, propagation, evidence, intervention points, uncertainty, and action-relative sufficiency.
theories.boundary: Coherence and internal representational utility are supported more strongly than comparative diagnostic performance.

theories.title: EDF-specific incremental diagnostic value
theories.statement: EDF-specific concepts provide semantic diagnostic value beyond a matched neutral structured prompt.
theories.boundary: No controlled matched-structure benchmark has been completed.

theories.title: Evidence provenance is part of framework validity
theories.statement: A framework-performance claim is not reconstructable from summary outputs alone; exact execution provenance, failures, raw outputs, and scoring are necessary to distinguish structural conformity from reproducible performance.
theories.boundary: This is a research-method principle derived from the repository's missing-provenance failure modes, not evidence that EDF itself performs better.
